notes: **READ ONLY — reported, not edited.** One finding: the module's own comment says *"the original's village carries no text at all"*, and that is false. `Village_Draw` makes three `Eng_DrawString` calls, all gated on `g_optAdvancedFarming == 1` — the same gate that moves `g_villageTopY` from 0x40 to 0x84 and loads `villtops.pl8`, which this module already reproduces as `draw_tops`. The words are `L2.eng` group 66 (twelve strings, six weather pairs: Frost / "- Many crops lost", Drought, Sunny / "- Boosts growing crops.", Cloudy, Storms, Flooding / "- All crops lost") and group 22 (seven fertility sentences, index `(fertility + 100) / 29`). The **colour is a rule**: `0x3F` for weather < 4 and `0x20` — the disabled grey — for Storms and Flooding, so the two worst kinds of weather are printed greyed out. Both facts are verified against the shipped `L2.eng` and the decompilation. Second, smaller: `Ui_OkButton(0x180, g_villageTopY + 0x118, 1)` is **mode 1**, System.pl8 frame 0x10, not the 0x33 the county panels use — this module already passes `OK_ALT`, which is right. Its literal inventory is left to the module's owner: the scanner sees one caption in village.rs, "CLOSE" at widget::button, and that one is an invention — Ui_OkButton(0x180, top + 0x118, **1**) draws System.pl8 frame 0x10 and no letters. Four more of ours reach text::draw_centred through a binding and are invisible to the scan: "CARRYING {n} - CLICK A JOB", "VILLAGE OF COUNTY {n}", "NO DROP GRID - VILL_GD8.PL8 MISSING" and "NOT YOURS", plus the eight JOB_NAMES in the no-artwork cluster fallback.
